request.spec:
A steward can merge a person into another (a select of the other person and a merge button on
the row; PERSON_MERGED from=<name> into=<name>; anyone else, the same person, or either of them
retired, is refused with an error on the row). The merged person's claims move to the other
(numbers and dates kept, listed after the other's claims in the order they were added, each losing
any figure a statement bound); the merged name and aliases become aliases of the other; the merged
person's patrons are added to the other's (not themselves, no repeats), anyone naming the merged
person as patron names the other instead (no repeats), and the merged person's pool memberships move
to the other (shares added when the other is already a member). Their statements, holds, watchers
and contact are dropped. The merged person leaves the list (no row), and every total follows.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A steward can merge a person into another (a select of the other person and a merge button on
the row; PERSON_MERGED from=<name> into=<name>; anyone else, the same person, or either of them
retired, is refused with an error on the row). The merged person's claims move to the other
(numbers and dates kept, listed after the other's claims in the order they were added, each losing
any figure a statement bound); the merged name and aliases become aliases of the other; the merged
person's patrons are added to the other's (not themselves, no repeats), anyone naming the merged
person as patron names the other instead (no repeats), and the merged person's pool memberships move
to the other (shares added when the other is already a member). Their statements, holds, watchers
and contact are dropped. The merged person leaves the list (no row), and every total follows.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
A steward can now merge one person into another. `bin/e2e` passes all four tests in the spec.

**How it works on screen:** each person's row has a "Merge into" select (`person-merge-into`) and a Merge button (`person-merge`). If the merge is refused, the message shows in the row's existing `person-error` element, and it clears on the next action on that row. If it goes through, the whole sheet is reloaded, because a merge changes people, claims, statements, patrons, pools and totals all at once.

**Server:** the merge is a new endpoint, `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/{id}/merge` with body `{ intoId }`, in `PersonController.java`. The logic is in a new `person/PersonMergeService.java` and runs in one transaction:
- **Refused** (nothing written) when the user isn't a steward, when merging a person into themselves, or when either person is retired.
- **Claims** move to the other person and keep their numbers and dates. Each loses any figure a statement bound it to. They're listed as the other person's newest claims, in the order they were added; this is the order the test expects.
- **Patrons:** the merged person's patrons go to the other person, skipping the other person themselves and any repeats. Anyone who named the merged person as patron now names the other person, again without repeats.
- **Pools:** the merged person's memberships move to the other person. Where the other person is already in a pool, the two shares are added together.
- **Dropped:** the merged person's statements and watchers are deleted, and the person record is then deleted, which takes their holds and contact with it.
- **Names:** the merged person's name and aliases become aliases of the other person.
- **Audit:** it writes `PERSON_MERGED sheet=… by=… from=<name> into=<name>`, followed by the usual ROLLUP/TOTALS lines for any figures that moved.

**Supporting changes:** `PoolMember` gained `moveTo` and `setShare`, and `PoolMemberRepository` gained two lookup methods. No database migration was needed.

**One thing a merge doesn't update:** per-person totals already stored for a period (the `period_person_total` table) aren't moved, so those figures will still show the merged person. The spec doesn't test this.
